stem: An individual with quadriplegia lacks motor function below the neck. Which assistive technology allows them to navigate digital interfaces independently?

options.text: A standard multi-touch trackpad built into the laptop's palm rest.
options.rationale: Standard trackpads require physical finger and hand dexterity.

options.text: An external high-contrast keyboard with large keycaps and wide spacing.
options.rationale: Keyboards require physical upper limb movement to press keys.

options.text: A sip-and-puff switch system combined with on-screen scanning software.
options.rationale: Sip-and-puff devices translate air pressure changes created by breathing through a mouth tube into digital commands.

options.text: A wearable wrist-mounted trackball controlled by deliberate arm movements.
options.rationale: Wrist trackballs require intentional arm or wrist motor movements.

explanation: Assistive technologies—including sip-and-puff switches, head wands, and eye-tracking cameras—allow individuals with limited or no functional limb movement to interact with digital operating systems and application software.
